# Probe mapping and replicate probes

Probes are mapped to hg38 CpG positions with a user-supplied or built-in
manifest. Probes without coordinates are dropped and counted. EPICv2 and
EPIC-Xtra include replicate probes (suffixes such as `_TC11`, `_BC11`) that
target the same CpG; they are averaged per sample (ignoring NA) **only when
their coordinates are identical**. Probes sharing a `cg` base name but mapped to
different positions are kept separate, because a shared name does not
guarantee a shared locus.

# CoRSIV definition and summary

CoRSIVs are taken from CoRSIV 2.0 (merged population-specific calls, hg38;
Gunasekara et al. 2019 for the original atlas). Each CoRSIV is identified by its
1-based coordinates (`chr:start-end`); the original merged names are retained
but are not unique and are never used as keys. A CoRSIV is analysed if it
contains at least `min_cpgs` (default 3) distinct CpGs on the array. For sample
*j* and CoRSIV *r* with measured CpGs *C_rj*,

$$\bar\beta_{rj} = \frac{1}{|C_{rj}|} \sum_{c \in C_{rj}} \beta_{cj}, \quad |C_{rj}| \ge \texttt{min\_cpgs},$$

and NA otherwise: a sample whose number of non-missing CpGs in the region falls
below `min_cpgs` gets NA for that region. Regions with more than `max_na_frac`
(default 0.2) NA samples are removed. The mean is used as the regional summary;
`fun = "median"` is available as a robust alternative (the same per-sample
`min_cpgs` rule applies).

# Differential methylation model

For each region the summary is converted to an M-value,
$M = \log_2\{\beta/(1-\beta)\}$ with $\beta$ clamped to $[10^{-6}, 1-10^{-6}]$,
and modelled with a linear model $M_r = X\gamma_r + \varepsilon_r$, where $X$ is
the user's design (e.g. `~ group + age + sex + cell fractions`). The model is
fitted with limma (`lmFit` followed by `eBayes` with `trend = TRUE` for the
mean–variance trend and `robust = TRUE` for robust hyperparameter estimation
that down-weights hypervariable regions; Smyth 2004; Phipson et al. 2016).
M-values are used for inference because their variance is approximately
homogeneous across the methylation range (Du et al. 2010); the reported effect
size, $\Delta\beta$, is the same design coefficient fitted on the beta scale.

**Blocks.** limma is fitted separately within the target set and within each
background draw. The variance prior (and its mean–variance trend) and the FDR
family are therefore block-specific, and target statistics do not depend on the
background chosen.

**Missing values.** Samples with a missing value in any design variable are
dropped (and counted); if the remaining samples do not exceed the number of
design columns, the analysis stops with an error. Within a block, a row is
reported with NA statistics, and is excluded from the variance prior and from
the BH family, if (i) its number of non-missing samples does not exceed the
number of design columns (no residual degrees of freedom), or (ii) its own
missing values leave some design column non-estimable (for example, every
sample of one group is missing for that row). The number of rows in case (ii)
is reported in a message.

**CpG-level analysis.** With `level = "cpg"`, each array CpG inside an analysed
CoRSIV is modelled separately with the same design and the same procedure. The
target block contains all target CpGs (FDR over target CpGs); background CpGs
form one block per background draw, or a single block of all eligible array
CpGs with `background = "array"`.

**Multiple testing.** Benjamini–Hochberg FDR is computed within the target set
only (and separately within each background draw). The FDR therefore refers to
the family of CoRSIV tests, not to the whole array; this is a deliberate
restriction of the hypothesis family and must be reported as such.

**Assumptions and limitations.** Independent samples (no repeated measures in
v0.1); approximately normal residuals on the M scale; covariates enter only
through the design. CoRSIVs are enriched for methylation QTLs, so genotype can
confound group comparisons — include ancestry PCs where available. chrX
CoRSIVs are excluded by default because their methylation differs by sex and
requires sex-stratified models.

# Background comparison

**Matched control regions.** For each of `n_draws` draws, each analysed CoRSIV
is paired with one random control region that has (1) the same width, (2) the
same number of array CpGs (exact when the target has fewer than 10, otherwise
±1), (3) the same chromosome type (autosome or chrX), and (4) CpG density (CpGs
per 100 bp, hg38) within $\pm\max(0.2d, 0.25)$ of the target's density $d$.
Controls are proposed by choosing a random array CpG outside every CoRSIV ±
`flank` bp on a chromosome of the target's type and placing a window of the
target's width at a uniformly random offset containing it. A proposal is
rejected if the window extends beyond the chromosome end, if any part of the
**whole window** lies within a CoRSIV ± `flank`, if it overlaps a control
already accepted in the same draw, or if it fails criteria (2) or (4);
proposals are repeated up to `max_tries` times per target per draw. This
follows the permutation-with-constraints approach of regioneR (Gel et al.
2016), adapted to array data: matching on probe count keeps the precision of
regional summaries comparable between targets and controls. Targets for which
no control is found in a draw are unmatched in that draw but remain in the
target statistic; `matchDiagnostics()` reports the number unmatched per draw
(on EPIC-Xtra, about 3.6–3.9% of 3,036 targets per draw, typically CpG-dense
ones), and a warning is given if more than 5% are unmatched in any draw.

**Seeds.** Draw $r$ ($r = 1, \dots, R$) is generated with random seed
`seed + r`. Results are reproducible for a given `seed`, but two analyses with
base seeds closer than `n_draws` share draws (for example, draw 2 of `seed = 1`
is draw 1 of `seed = 2`). For an independent sensitivity analysis, use base
seeds that differ by at least `n_draws` (e.g. `seed = 1` and `seed = 1001` with
100 draws).

**Array background.** With `background = "array"` (CpG level only), the
background is every array CpG outside all CoRSIVs ± `flank`, restricted to the
chromosome types of the targets (autosomes by default, so chrX, chrY,
mitochondrial and unplaced-contig CpGs are excluded). It is a single block
(one "draw").

**Statistics.** The enrichment statistic for a set is the fraction $f$ of
tested regions (or CpGs) with $P <$ `p` (default 0.05). For matched draws, the
empirical p-value is one-sided (target at least as enriched as background),
$(1 + \#\{r : f_r \ge f_{target}\})/(1 + R)$ over $R$ draws (Phipson & Smyth
2010), and is reported only when $R \ge 20$; in matched mode this empirical p
is the primary inference. The same one-sided empirical procedure is applied to
the median between-individual SD of beta, as a data-quality check: CoRSIVs are
expected to be more variable between individuals than matched control regions.
Fisher's exact test (two-sided) of target versus pooled background is also
reported. It treats all background units as independent, although controls
from different draws can reuse the same loci and, in `"array"` mode, roughly a
million spatially correlated CpGs enter the test; it is therefore
anti-conservative and should be read as descriptive.

- Du P, et al. (2010) Comparison of Beta-value and M-value methods for quantifying methylation levels by microarray analysis. *BMC Bioinformatics* 11:587.
- Gel B, et al. (2016) regioneR: an R/Bioconductor package for the association analysis of genomic regions based on permutation tests. *Bioinformatics* 32:289–291.
- Gunasekara CJ, et al. (2019) A genomic atlas of systemic interindividual epigenetic variation in humans. *Genome Biology* 20:105.
